canh: the garden of the Navy Office, London, 4 September 1666: burying wine and a cheese
loi_cau: In the west, the fire crosses the Fleet and runs down Fleet Street, as far as the Temple. Only now are houses blown up with gunpowder to open firebreaks — first in Tower Street, near the Tower. At the Navy Office, Pepys and a colleague dig a pit in the garden for their wine — and Pepys buries his Parmesan cheese. In the last days of the fire, the King and the Duke work the fire-lines themselves — “even laboring in person,” Evelyn writes.
mo_ta: Samuel Pepys and a colleague bury wine bottles and a wheel of cheese in a garden while the Great Fire of London blazes against the night sky in the background.
